title: 3D model
prompt: Make a 3D model that, if everyone saw it, would improve the world for the greatest number of people.
final_prompt:
Make a 3D model that, if everyone saw it, would improve the world for the greatest number of people.

Make it in Blender, working in the current directory.
- A Blender 5 instance is running for you with no window (background mode). Use it through the `blender`
  MCP tools: run Python (`bpy`) with execute_blender_code, and look things up with the API and manual
  search tools. Blender's working directory is the current directory. The scene starts as Blender's
  default one (a cube, a camera and a light).
- There is no window to screenshot. To check your work, render it to an image file and look at the image
  (render_thumbnail_to_path, render_viewport_to_path, or a render of the scene camera to a file).
  Keep renders quick: a single tool call may take at most 5 minutes. Save what you look at as .jpg rather
  than .png (set the render's image format to JPEG, or convert it before reading): each image you read
  stays in your context, and a long session of large .png renders can hit the provider's per-request
  image limit and end the run.
- Build it in Blender itself; don't write the model or the images any other way.
- Save the finished result in ./output/ (only what is in ./output/ is published):
  - the model or scene as one .glb file (glTF binary), shown on the site in an interactive 3D viewer:
    `bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(filepath=..., export_format='GLB')`, without Draco or meshopt
    compression, at most 15 MB;
  - one or more final renders as .png or .jpg, at most 2 MB each, from camera angles you choose.
  At most 8 files in all.
- Tools available on this machine: python3 3.12.13 (standard library only), node 24.18.0 (no npm packages), ffmpeg 8.1.1, ffprobe 8.1.1. Don't install packages or download anything (no asset
  libraries or add-ons).
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory.
- Finish with a short summary of what you made.

runs.summary: Oral Rehydration Solution is a 3D recipe equation for the home-mixed drink that treats dehydration from diarrhea, a leading killer of young children. Carved into a clay tablet readable in any language, it shows one litre of clean water, six level teaspoons of sugar and half a teaspoon of salt, so anyone can see how simple a life-saving remedy can be.

A tabletop diorama that teaches how to make oral rehydration solution at home, a simple mix of clean water, sugar and salt that can save a child from dehydration caused by diarrhoea. Five numbered steps run left to right, from measuring one litre of water, six level teaspoons of sugar and half a teaspoon of salt, through stirring, to a caregiver giving small sips from a cup. A backboard gives the guidance in plain terms, along with the warning signs that mean a child needs medical help at once.

The Common Table is a 3D model of a welcoming circle beneath a fruit tree, where people share food, water and learning, with an empty chair left open for whoever arrives next. It shows generosity as an everyday practice, and that a place of plenty can be made for everyone.

Common Ground is a 3D model of five ceramic hands holding up a living Earth, with an open circle around it that invites others to join. Its inscription reads "No one thrives alone," making a quiet case that everyone's wellbeing depends on one another.

The World in a Drop of Water is a stone-and-glass monument: a large, clear droplet hangs above a still stone basin, with the Earth magnified inside it as if seen through a lens. It argues that clean water sustains life for everyone, and that safe drinking water is among the surest ways to improve the lives of the most people.

The Overview is a portrait of Earth as the one borderless home everyone shares, rendered as an interactive 3D model with drifting clouds, a thin blue atmosphere and the Moon beside it. It is built to recreate the overview effect, the sense of seeing the planet whole that makes it feel singular, fragile and shared.

The Commons of Life is an interactive 3D cutaway sanctuary that gathers everyday life-saving know-how into one model. A rainwater cistern feeds four stations: water purification, oral rehydration and handwashing, CPR and the recovery position, and a smoke-free rocket stove beside a keyhole compost garden.

Held in Common is a fountain sculpture of open hands, of different ages and skin tones, rising from a single pool to cradle a living Earth, with a young olive tree growing from its top. It argues that the world is not something to grab but something held together, and it leaves a gap in the circle for a visitor's own hand.

Common Ground is a 3D sculpture of twelve diverse people, a child and a wheelchair user among them, joining hands around the Earth beneath a flourishing tree and three doves. It stands for shared stewardship, inclusion, cooperation and peace.

One Home: The Pale Blue Dot is a 3D sculpture of Earth as a single borderless sphere suspended in darkness, with Carl Sagan's words on a floating gold-inscribed plaque beside it. Seen whole from space, the planet shows no nations or borders, only one fragile blue world, a view meant to shift perspective for anyone, whatever their language, politics or beliefs.

A solar-powered community water station named SOLAQUA, built as a scalable public-service hub. It collects rainwater into a cistern, shades visitors under a dual solar-panel canopy, and offers an accessible filtered drinking fountain with a visible water-level indicator. Its phone-charging ledge, warm night lighting, public information board, and tactile paving make it a place where a neighborhood can get clean water, power, and information.

"One Shared Home" is a 3D public sculpture of a stylised Earth rising like a sprouting plant, crowned with a red heart and a golden ring of doves. Twelve diverse figures, including a child, an elder with a cane, and a wheelchair user, stand hand in hand in an unbroken circle around the planet, with trees and a plaza plinth beneath them. Its message is that there is one planet and everyone belongs in the circle of care.
